source_title: Shimla-Bilaspur-Dharamshala highway closed for repairs, NHAI issues traffic advisory - ET TravelWorld
source_excerpt: The road at this location in Namhol (Bilaspur) on the Shimla-Dharamshala National Highway will remain closed until the repair work is completed.The Shimla-Bilaspur-Dharamshala national highway, connecting the capital city to the state's nine districts, has been closed for repair work following road subsidence, officials said on Tuesday.The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) had closed this stretch for all vehicles, both small and large on October 27, an official spokesman said in a statement. However, the strech opened for light vehicle movemebt on same day at 4:00 pm.In response, the NHAI and the office of the Bilaspur Superintendent of Police have issued an advisory, providing alternative routes for travellers and urging motorists to use designated routes and follow traffic instructions.One way light vehicle flow eases car trips but leaves buses and goods carriers diverted, so group tours must still reroute.The police have designated an alternative route for vehicles travelling from Bilaspur and Hamirpur toward Shimla. These vehicles will travel via Barmana, Jukhala, Jwal Pul, Ranikotal, Gharsi, and Darlaghat to reach Shimla.Similarly, vehicles travelling from Shimla toward Bilaspur and Hamirpur may proceed via Darlaghat, Gharsi, Ranikotal, Jwal Pul, and Ghumarwin/Barmana.Tourists visiting destinations such as Shimla, Kasauli, Chail, Narkanda, and Kufri -- many of whom use this national highway to travel onward to places like Manali, Dharamshala, and Rohtang -- must also follow this advisory, it said.The road at this location in Namhol (Bilaspur) on the Shimla-Dharamshala National Highway will remain closed until the repair work is completed.Vehicles travelling from Shimla towards Mandi are advised to take a route passing through Darlaghat, Navgaon, Gharsi, Ranikotal and Bairi.Directives have also been issued to prioritise emergency vehicles. The stretch reopens fully only after repairs are complete.Until the necessary road improvement work is completed, heavy vehicles should plan their journeys according to these alternative routes, the spokesman said.
